method: A uniform linear array of N equal-amplitude elements spaced d wavelengths apart, with a linear phase progression chosen to point the main beam at the steering angle theta0, has the array factor |sin(N psi/2) / (N sin(psi/2))| with psi = 2 pi (d/lambda)(sin theta - sin theta0); the tool evaluates this pattern from -90 to 90 degrees around broadside. The peak gain over a single element is 10 log10 N. The half-power beamwidth is found by scanning the pattern outward from the steering angle in 0.01 degree steps and interpolating the first -3 dB crossings on both sides; it is reported only when both crossings lie inside the visible range and is otherwise marked as clipped. The first sidelobe is the highest point of the lobe between the first and second nulls of the array factor, located by a golden-section search in psi and reported with the angle where it appears; it is suppressed when that lobe falls outside visible space or when the peak sits on the next main-lobe replica, which is what a two-element array at half-wave spacing shows. Nulls fall at sin theta = sin theta0 plus or minus lambda/(N d). Grating lobes appear at sin theta = sin theta0 + m lambda/d for every non-zero integer m whose angle lies inside the range, which is why a spacing wider than 1/(1 + |sin theta0|) wavelengths produces them. Elements are integers from 2 to 64, spacing is 0.05 to 5 wavelengths and steering is -90 to 90 degrees; blank, non-numeric or out-of-range values are rejected with a message naming the field rather than defaulted. Elements are ideal isotropic radiators of equal amplitude: element patterns, mutual coupling, amplitude taper, nulling weights, scan loss, phase-shifter quantisation, near-field effects and hardware errors are not modelled, and the result is the array factor alone rather than a measured antenna pattern. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: For N equal-amplitude elements with a linear phase progression the array factor is |sin(N psi/2) / (N sin(psi/2))| with psi = 2 pi (d/lambda)(sin theta - sin theta0), and its peak gain over one element is 10 log10 N.

Grating lobes repeat the main beam at sin theta = sin theta0 + m lambda/d, so a spacing of one wavelength or more can put a full-strength lobe inside visible space; the largest spacing that avoids one at steering angle theta0 is d/lambda = 1/(1 + |sin theta0|).
The first sidelobe of a uniform array approaches 20 log10(1/(N sin(3 pi / 2N))), about -13.3 dB as N grows, and the half-power beamwidth of a broadside array is roughly 0.886 lambda/(N d) radians.
Nulls of the uniform array factor fall at sin theta = sin theta0 plus or minus lambda/(N d) and repeat every lambda/(N d) in sin theta, which sets the null-to-null beamwidth reported here.
